provenance.notes: Pin map and package: Kingbright DC10EWA 10 segment bar graph array (spec DSAD1426 rev V.10A), page 1 package drawing and internal circuit: ten independent LEDs, LED n between pin n (anode, pins 1 to 10 along one row, anode mark at pin 1) and pin 21 - n (cathode, pins 11 to 20 along the other row; LED 1 is pins 1 and 20, LED 10 is pins 10 and 11). The datasheet gives pin numbers only, so the labels A1 to A10 (pins 1 to 10) and K10 to K1 (pins 11 to 20) are named for this file. Numbering is counter-clockwise from pin 1 at the bottom left of the top view (pins 1 to 10 along the bottom, 11 to 20 back along the top). Body 25.4 x 10.16 mm, about 8 mm high with leads 4 +/- 0.5 mm long and 0.5 mm in diameter, 2.54 mm pin pitch, rows 7.5 mm apart (the recommended PCB layout; 3 breadboard pitches is 7.62 mm). Segment window 24.64 mm long (9 x 2.54 + 1.78), segments 1.78 x 5.08 mm. Ratings (page 2): VF 1.9 V typical and 2.3 V maximum at 10 mA, DC IF 30 mA, peak IF 160 mA at 1/10 duty and 0.1 ms, VR 5 V; these are the DC10EWA high-efficiency-red chip. Kit status: the component-list image shows "LED Bar Graph x1", and the photo on SunFounder's page 1.3.3 shows the body marked 2510SR-1 (the schematic image led_bar_sche.png numbers its pins 1 to 10 on one side and 11 to 20 on the other, with the anode end of each LED on pins 1 to 10). No datasheet for the 2510SR-1 marking was found, so its dimensions, VF and ratings are unverified; the Kingbright part is the pin-compatible datasheet. SunFounder's code turns a segment on by driving its GPIO low and its comments call this "common anode"; that describes the wiring (the GPIOs sit on the cathode side), since the ten LEDs share no pin. The page maps segment 1 to 10 to GPIO17, 18, 27, 22, 23, 24, 25, SDA1, SCL1, SPICE0 and does not say which physical LED each is.
